              adult: "Replay the recorded episodes on the robot and compare its behavior against the demonstration, then deploy a trained policy for the first rollout and observe the result." },
        13: { kids: "Now the robot learns for real. The computer studies all your good examples, again and again. It learns how the job is done. What it learns is saved as a policy. That policy came from YOUR examples.",
              teen: "You manage the dataset and train an AI policy from your own demonstrations on a classroom computer — GPU, Mac, or CPU — logging the training choices you make.",
              adult: "Manage the class dataset and train an AI policy from the students' own demonstrations (GPU, Mac, or CPU), with the training choices logged for iteration." },
        14: { kids: "This is the big show. The robot does the whole job by itself. No steering. No help. Just what YOU taught it. Then you tell everyone how you built it and how you taught it. You did this!",
              teen: "Final rollout: Sourccey performs the class task on its own, and each team presents what it built and taught — build log and dataset included.",
              adult: "Final rollout: Sourccey performs the class task autonomously; each team presents its build log and dataset — an account of what it built and what it taught the robot." }
      };
      window.__suTrack = window.__suTrack || 'teen';
      window.__suSetTrack = function (key) {
        if (key !== 'kids' && key !== 'teen' && key !== 'adult') return;
        window.__suTrack = key;
        if (document.body) document.body.classList.toggle('su-track-kids', key === 'kids');
        document.querySelectorAll('.nc-mu-t').forEach(function (el) {
          var ex = EXPLAIN[el.getAttribute('data-lesson')];
          if (ex) el.textContent = ex[key];
        });
      };

      function lessonHTML(L, pc){
        var steps = L.steps.map(function(s, i){
          var stage = s.stage ? ' <span class="nc-stage">· ' + s.stage + '</span>' : '';
          return '<li><span class="nc-step-n">' + (i+1) + '</span><div class="nc-step-t">' + s.t + stage + '</div><div class="nc-step-d">' + s.d + '</div></li>';
        }).join('');
        var extra = '';
        if (L.cleanBar){
          extra = '<div class="nc-sub-block"><div class="nc-db-h">A CLEAN EPISODE — THE BAR</div>' +
            '<p>An episode counts as clean only if all four hold:</p><ul>' +
            '<li>the robot starts from a consistent start position;</li>' +
            '<li>the whole task stays in frame;</li>' +
            '<li>there are no mid-task corrections;</li>' +
            '<li>the task is carried through to a completed finish.</li></ul>' +
            '<p style="margin-top:6px;">Anything less is discarded and re-recorded — it does not count toward the 5.</p></div>';
        }
        if (L.clinic){
          extra = '<div class="nc-sub-block"><div class="nc-db-h">TROUBLESHOOTING CLINIC — USE AFTER LESSON 9</div>' +
            '<p>First power-up is where the build tells the truth. Work this table in order — symptom, check, fix — before changing anything else. Power off before any hands-on fix, per Safety &amp; Care.</p>' +
            '<div class="nc-clinic-wrap"><table class="nc-clinic-table"><tr><th>Symptom</th><th>Check</th><th>Fix</th></tr>' +
            '<tr><td>A device does not report in</td><td>Re-run Lesson 9\'s device verification, device by device, out loud, from the top.</td><td>Stop and diagnose — do not carry a silent device into calibration. The answer is almost always a Lesson 7 cable or an unset servo ID.</td></tr>' +
            '<tr><td>Servo ID conflict — the wrong joint answers, or joints answer together</td><td>Check the servo IDs against the motor-ID programming from Lesson 7 (Stages 1–3): IDs must be set before the arms connect.</td><td>Reset the conflicting ID, verify it, and only then reconnect.</td></tr>' +
            '<tr><td>A device drops out, or works only sometimes</td><td>Power off, then check that run\'s cable: is the connector fully seated, and is the cable labeled and routed as it was laid in Lesson 7?</td><td>Reseat the connector, compare the run against the manual\'s routing, then re-verify the device.</td></tr>' +
            '<tr><td>Battery gauge reads abnormally</td><td>Read the gauge before anything else and say the reading out loud, as at every power-up.</td><td>A pack that is swollen, punctured, hot, or reading abnormally comes out of service and goes to the teacher immediately — and packs are charged only with the chargers included in the kit.</td></tr>' +
            '</table></div><p style="margin-top:8px;"><b style="color:var(--nc-txt);">The clinic rule:</b> stop and diagnose. A fault found here is the lesson, not an interruption of it — and no fix moves the class past a checkoff that has not passed.</p></div>';
        }
        var phaseName = PHASES[L.phase - 1].name;
        return '<div class="nc-lesson" style="--ncpc:' + pc + '">' +
          '<button class="nc-lesson-bar" aria-expanded="false">' +
            '<span class="nc-orb">' + L.n + '</span>' +
            '<span class="nc-bar-main"><span class="nc-bar-kicker">Phase ' + L.phase + ' · ' + phaseName + ' — Lesson ' + L.n + ' of 14</span>' +
            '<span class="nc-bar-title">' + L.title + '</span>' +
            '<span class="nc-bar-tag">' + L.ref + '</span></span>' +
            '<span class="nc-chev">' + CHEV_SVG + '</span>' +
          '</button>' +
          '<div class="nc-lesson-body"><div class="nc-lesson-inner"><div class="nc-lesson-detail">' +
            '<span class="nc-manual-ref">' + (/^Manual/.test(L.ref) ? 'Assembly Manual · ' : 'Reference · ') + L.ref.replace(/^Manual · |^Software · |^SDK path · /, '') + '</span>' +
            manChipHTML(L) +
            '<div class="nc-pacing-meta"><span><b>Pacing</b>&ensp;' + L.pacing + '</span></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-goal-line"><b>GOAL</b>' + L.goal + '</div>' +
            '<div class="nc-mu-explain"><div class="nc-mu-h">MU EXPLAINS IT</div><div class="nc-mu-t" data-lesson="' + L.n + '">' + (EXPLAIN[L.n] ? EXPLAIN[L.n][window.__suTrack] : '') + '</div></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block" style="margin-top:0;"><div class="nc-db-h">STEP BY STEP — IN THE MANUAL\'S ORDER</div>' +
            '<ol class="nc-steps">' + steps + '</ol></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block"><div class="nc-db-h">KEY SKILLS</div><div class="nc-skill-chips">' +
              L.skills.map(function(s){ return '<span>' + s + '</span>'; }).join('') + '</div></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block"><div class="nc-db-h">TEACHER NOTES</div><div class="nc-teacher-note">' + L.teacher + '</div></div>' +
            extra +
            '<div class="nc-done-step"><span class="nc-done-check">' + CHECK_SVG + '</span><div>' +
              '<div class="nc-dt">FINAL STEP — DONE LOOKS LIKE · THE CHECKOFF</div><div class="nc-dd">' + L.done + '</div></div></div>' +
          '</div></div></div></div>';
      }

      function safetyHTML(){
        return '<div class="nc-lesson nc-xbar" style="--ncpc:var(--nc-gold)">' +
          '<button class="nc-lesson-bar" aria-expanded="false">' +
            '<span class="nc-orb">!</span>' +
            '<span class="nc-bar-main"><span class="nc-bar-title">Before Lesson 1 — Safety &amp; Care</span>' +
            '<span class="nc-bar-tag">Read before Lesson 1 · five rules, enforced every session</span></span>' +
            '<span class="nc-chev">' + CHEV_SVG + '</span></button>' +
          '<div class="nc-lesson-body"><div class="nc-lesson-inner"><div class="nc-lesson-detail">' +
            '<span class="nc-manual-ref">Program Requirement · Read before Lesson 1</span>' +
            '<div class="nc-pacing-meta"><span><b>Applies</b>&ensp;Every session, Lessons 1–14&ensp;|&ensp;Posted in the room</span></div>' +
            '<p style="color:var(--nc-mut); font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.65;">Sourccey is a real machine — about a metre tall, with powered arms, a lift, and a lithium battery. These five rules are not suggestions. The teacher states them in Lesson 1, posts them in the room, and enforces them in every session that follows.</p>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>1 · Soldering is teacher-led</b><p>One step in the whole build uses a soldering iron: the potentiometer wires, in Lesson 7. It is done teacher-led, with gloves and ventilation, exactly as the Assembly Manual shows. Students prepare, hold, and inspect; the teacher runs the iron. No other lesson involves soldering, and the iron is never left unattended or passed hand to hand.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>2 · Battery discipline</b><p>The robot runs on a LiFePO4 battery pack. Charge it only with the chargers included in the kit — never a substitute charger. At every power-up, check the battery gauge before doing anything else, and say the reading out loud so the whole team hears it. A pack that is swollen, punctured, hot, or reading abnormally comes out of service and goes to the teacher immediately.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>3 · No adhesives on structural joints</b><p>If a joint does not fit, the fix is mechanical: unbolt it and refit it. Glue and tape on a structural joint hide a misalignment, make the next stage harder, and turn a five-minute refit into a broken part. Adhesives stay out of the build unless the manual itself calls for them.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>4 · Two-person lift, power off</b><p>Built, Sourccey weighs 15.88 kg. Moving it is always a two-person lift, and the robot is powered off before it is moved every time, even across the room. Lift from the base, never by the arms, dome, or lift.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>5 · Driving sessions are supervised</b><p>Driving Sourccey (Lesson 10) is always supervised: one driver at a time, a cleared drive area, and the robot\'s off switch within the teacher\'s reach.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block"><div class="nc-db-h">CARE OF THE MACHINE</div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>Power off before hands-on work</b><p>Any time hands go inside the body — wiring, refits, inspection — the robot is off first.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>Know the off switch</b><p>From Lesson 9 onward, every student must be able to find and use the power-off switch without looking it up. The teacher checks this; it is part of the Lesson 9 checkoff.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>Servos are not hand-cranks</b><p>Outside the hand tests the lessons specify, joints are moved by the controls, not forced by hand.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>Epoxy work follows the manual\'s PPE</b><p>The wheel housings (Lesson 1, Manual Stage 0) are bonded with structural epoxy. While it is uncured it releases fumes: nitrile gloves, a face mask rated for organic fumes, and a well-ventilated area, exactly as the manual\'s safety note requires — and the bonded housings cure for at least an hour before they carry any load.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>End every session tidy</b><p>Parts back in their tray zone, cables as the manual routes them, build log updated. The next session starts from a known state.</p></div></div>' +
          '</div></div></div></div>';
      }

            '<p style="color:var(--nc-mut); font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.65;">Assessment rests on evidence the class produces as it goes — not on a final test. Three sources, all already in the room:</p>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>The 14 checkoffs</b><p>Every lesson\'s Done looks like is a checkpoint — 14 in total. Each is observable (rolls freely, calibration saved, 5 clean episodes) and signed off at the end of its lesson, while the evidence is still on the bench. A missed checkoff is fixed in the next session\'s open, before new work begins.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>The build log</b><p>Each team keeps a build log across all 14 lessons: times, refits, decisions, training choices. The log shows process — how a team worked, what it caught, what it fixed — which the finished robot alone cannot show.</p></div>' +

It is graded on the honesty and specificity of the account, not on a flawless final run.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block"><div class="nc-db-h">TRACK DEPTH CHART — SAME ROBOT, THREE DEPTHS</div>' +

            '<tr><td>Project</td><td>Guided team project, built from the class datasets</td><td>Team project with own training runs</td><td>Original research project</td></tr>' +
            '<tr><td>Finish</td><td>Trained policy + team presentation</td><td>Trained policy + full presentation</td><td>Trained policy + research write-up</td></tr></table></div>' +
            '<p style="color:var(--nc-mut); font-size:14px; line-height:1.6; margin-top:10px;">Every track builds the same robot, passes the same 14 checkoffs, and finishes with the same Lesson 14 solo performance. A younger student is not building a lesser machine — they are building the same machine with more of the room\'s help, and they meet the full depth when they return in an older track.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-detail-block"><div class="nc-db-h">BETWEEN SESSIONS</div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>Practise in the simulators</b><p>Sourccey has full simulators — MuJoCo and Isaac Sim — with the complete robot: arms, grippers, elevator, and mecanum drive, with interactive controls. Between sessions, students practise driving in simulation, where a mistake costs nothing and the real robot stays exactly as the last checkoff left it. Simulator time is also the answer for early finishers and snow days.</p></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-rule-item"><b>MAKER classes print one stage ahead</b><p>For MAKER classes, the print queue runs one stage ahead of the lessons: while the class builds Stage N, the printer produces Stage N+1. Parts are checked against the print queue as they come off the printer, so a failed print is discovered a week before its lesson — not during it. COMPLETE classes have no queue to run; their between-session work is the simulators and the build log.</p></div></div>' +

And the experience the whole program is pointed at: standing in a room, hands off, watching a machine perform a task — because they taught it to.</p></div>' +

      /* ============ RENDER ============ */
      (function render(){
        var mount = document.getElementById('ncCoursesMount');
        var html = safetyHTML();
        PHASES.forEach(function(P){
          var pOpen = P.n === 1;
          html += '<div class="nc-phase-sec' + (pOpen ? ' nc-phase-open' : '') + '" style="--ncpc:' + P.color + '">' +
            '<button class="nc-phase-sec-head" type="button" aria-expanded="' + (pOpen ? 'true' : 'false') + '"><span class="nc-phase-tag">PHASE ' + P.n + '</span><span class="nc-phase-name">' + P.name + '</span><span class="nc-pr">' + P.range + '</span><span class="nc-chev">' + CHEV_SVG + '</span></button>' +
            '<div class="nc-phase-body"><div class="nc-phase-inner">' +
            '<div class="nc-phase-rule"></div>' +
            '<div class="nc-phase-meta"><span>' + P.count + '</span><span>' + P.stages + '</span></div>' +
            '<p class="nc-pintro">' + P.intro + '</p>';
          LESSONS.filter(function(L){ return L.phase === P.n; }).forEach(function(L){
            html += lessonHTML(L, P.color);
            if (L.n === 7){
              html += '<div class="nc-checkpoint"><b>Phase 1 checkpoint — before any power.</b> Seven checkoffs passed: base, body, lift, two arms, dome, wiring. The robot is complete as a machine and has never been switched on. Phase 2 begins with software — and the first power-up is its own lesson, with its own safety checks, not a moment at the end of a build day.</div>';
            }
          });
          html += '</div></div></div>';
        });
        html += '<div style="margin-top:26px;">' + assessmentHTML() + '</div>';
        mount.innerHTML = html;

        mount.addEventListener('click', function(e){
          var chip = e.target.closest('.nc-man-chip');
          if (chip) { openManualAtPage(parseInt(chip.getAttribute('data-man-page'), 10)); return; }
          var phead = e.target.closest('.nc-phase-sec-head');
          if (phead) {
            var psec = phead.closest('.nc-phase-sec');
            var pNowOpen = psec.classList.toggle('nc-phase-open');
            phead.setAttribute('aria-expanded', pNowOpen ? 'true' : 'false');
            return;
          }
          var bar = e.target.closest('.nc-lesson-bar');
          if (!bar) return;
          var lesson = bar.closest('.nc-lesson');
          var open = lesson.classList.toggle('nc-open');
          bar.setAttribute('aria-expanded', open ? 'true' : 'false');
        });
      })();

      /* ============ SHEET OPEN / CLOSE ============ */
      var sheet = document.getElementById('ncCoursesSheet');
      function openSheet(){
        document.getElementById('ncSheetBody').scrollTop = 0;
        sheet.classList.add('nc-open');
                document.getElementById('ncCloseCourses').focus({ preventScroll:true });
      }
      function closeSheet(){
        sheet.classList.remove('nc-open');
                document.getElementById('ncOpenCourses').focus({ preventScroll:true });
      }
      document.getElementById('ncOpenCourses').addEventListener('click', openSheet);
      document.getElementById('ncCloseCourses').addEventListener('click', closeSheet);
      document.getElementById('ncContentsCourses').addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.preventDefault(); openSheet(); });
      window.__ncForceCloseCourses = function () { sheet.classList.remove('nc-open'); };
      // Layered Escape: with the manual closed, Escape closes only the
      // courses sheet (capture phase, ahead of the page's sheet handler);
      // with the manual open, the page handler closes its sheets and the
      // observer below closes the courses with them.
      document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
        if (e.key !== 'Escape') return;
        var man = document.getElementById('sheet-manual');
        if (man && man.classList.contains('show')) return;
        if (sheet.classList.contains('nc-open')) { closeSheet(); e.stopPropagation(); }
      }, true);
      var currOverlay = document.getElementById('sheet-curriculum');
      if (window.MutationObserver && currOverlay) {
        new MutationObserver(function () {
          if (!currOverlay.classList.contains('show')) window.__ncForceCloseCourses();
        }).observe(currOverlay, { attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['class'] });
      }
      })();
    </script>
    <script>
      /* Netlify badge relocation — Netlify's HUD injects its
         "Powered by Netlify" badge as a fixed bottom-right iframe
         (#nl-badge-frame) after load, where it covers the Ask
         Sourccey chat corner. This moves that iframe, the moment it
         appears, into the in-flow slot at the bottom of the footer,
         where it scrolls with the page and can overlay nothing.
         On any serving where the iframe never appears (the Muse
         preview, local files), this is a complete no-op. */
      (function () {
        var slot = document.getElementById("nl-badge-slot");
        if (!slot) return;
        var done = false;
        function relocate() {
          var frame = document.getElementById("nl-badge-frame");
          if (!frame) return false;
          if (frame.parentNode !== slot) slot.appendChild(frame);
          frame.style.position = "static";
          frame.style.left = "auto";
          frame.style.right = "auto";
          frame.style.top = "auto";
          frame.style.bottom = "auto";
          frame.style.transform = "none";
          frame.style.zIndex = "auto";
          done = true;
          return true;
        }
        if (relocate()) return;
        var mo = null;
        if (window.MutationObserver) {
          mo = new MutationObserver(function () {
            if (relocate() && mo) { mo.disconnect(); mo = null; }
          });
          mo.observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
        }
        var tries = 0;
        var iv = setInterval(function () {
          tries++;
          if (relocate() || tries >= 120) {
            clearInterval(iv);
            if (mo) { mo.disconnect(); mo = null; }
          }
        }, 500);
        setTimeout(function () {
          if (!done && mo) { mo.disconnect(); mo = null; }
        }, 65000);
      })();
    </script>
    <script>
      (function () {
        // LOWER-SECTION TABS — Support, Stated Plainly / After 14
        // Lessons, Students Can / FAQs. Each tab starts CLOSED in
        // the markup (a slim pill in the tab rail — see the slim tab
        // rail addendum); tapping its heading opens the whole card
        // and tapping again collapses it back to the pill. This wiring lives in its OWN
        // script block, last on the page, so a fault anywhere else can
        // never take these toggles down, and it is the ONLY handler on
        // these three buttons (the old handlers in the shared shop
        // script were removed — a second handler would toggle twice
        // per tap and read as broken). The region's .open class is the
        // single source of truth; aria-expanded and the section's
        // .is-collapsed class are kept in sync by setLower(). The
        // WHOLE heading block (.sec-head — heading, padding, and the
        // divider rule) forwards taps to the button, so the tap lands
        // anywhere on the heading, not just on the text glyphs.
        function wireLower(toggleId) {
          var btn = document.getElementById(toggleId);
          if (!btn) return null;
          var region = document.getElementById(btn.getAttribute('aria-controls') || '');
          if (!region) return null;
          var section = btn.closest('section');
          var head = btn.closest('.sec-head');
          function setLower(open) {
            region.classList.toggle('open', open);
            btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(open));
            if (section) section.classList.toggle('is-collapsed', !open);
          }
          function syncLower() { setLower(region.classList.contains('open')); }
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            setLower(!region.classList.contains('open'));
          });
          if (head) {
            head.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
              if (e.target === btn || btn.contains(e.target)) return;
              btn.click();
            });
          }
          syncLower();
          return setLower;
        }
        var setSupportCard = wireLower('supportToggle');
        var setOutcomesCard = wireLower('outcomesToggle');
        wireLower('classesToggle');
        // A jump to a lower heading (a link to its id, or arriving
        // with that hash) opens that card on arrival, so linked
        // content is never hidden behind a collapsed heading.
        function openLowerFromHash() {
          var h = window.location.hash;
          if (h === '#support-h' && setSupportCard) setSupportCard(true);
          else if (h === '#outcomes-h' && setOutcomesCard) setOutcomesCard(true);
          else if (h === '#classes-h') {
            var t = document.getElementById('classesToggle');
            var r = document.getElementById('classesRegion');
            if (t && r && !r.classList.contains('open')) t.click();
          }
        }
        window.addEventListener('hashchange', openLowerFromHash);
        openLowerFromHash();
      })();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
